sources.entry: Unmanic | Library optimiser that automatically transcodes your media files

summary.one_liner: Unmanic is a library optimiser that scans and watches your media files and transcodes or otherwise processes them according to configured file presets.
summary.what_it_does: Unmanic scans a whole file library on a schedule and queues files that do not match configured presets. It also monitors directories so that modified or newly added files are tested against the same presets and queued if they need processing. A handler runs multiple file manipulation tasks at once. A Web UI is provided to configure, manage and monitor the optimisation progress. The README gives examples such as transcoding video or audio with FFmpeg, removing commercials from DVR recordings, moving files after a set period, running FileBot renames, compressing old files, and running custom commands on files by extension or size.
use_cases: transcode media library to a uniform format
automatically convert new video files on arrival
move files after a set age
compress files older than a certain age
run custom commands on files over a size threshold
how_to_run: Run 'python3 -m pip install -r requirements.txt' from the project root
Open a web browser to the address shown in the README (not specified)
notable: Scheduled library scans plus real-time file/directory monitoring
Plugin-based presets and custom commands per file
Built-in Web UI for configuration and progress monitoring
Runs multiple file tasks concurrently through a queue
caveats: You must install dependencies for any custom commands you configure
README defers up-to-date installation instructions to external Unmanic documentation
Source install requires git submodules and a manual setup.py install
keywords: convert my files to one format
